## Classes

### <a name="omsa"></a>`omsa`

Adds Dell's package repository, installs the OMSA packages, optionally sets
storage service options and keeps the OMSA services running. By default the
class only acts on physical Dell servers, so it can be included everywhere.

#### Examples

##### Include it on every host; only physical Dell servers get OMSA

```puppet
include omsa
```

##### Report alerts for drives that Dell hasn't certified

```puppet
class { 'omsa':
  non_dell_certified_flag => false,
}
```

##### Use a local mirror of Dell's repository

```puppet
class { 'omsa':
  manage_repo => false,
}
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `omsa` class:

* [`manage`](#-omsa--manage)
* [`manage_repo`](#-omsa--manage_repo)
* [`manage_service`](#-omsa--manage_service)
* [`package_names`](#-omsa--package_names)
* [`package_ensure`](#-omsa--package_ensure)
* [`service_names`](#-omsa--service_names)
* [`service_ensure`](#-omsa--service_ensure)
* [`service_enable`](#-omsa--service_enable)
* [`non_dell_certified_flag`](#-omsa--non_dell_certified_flag)

##### <a name="-omsa--manage"></a>`manage`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to manage OMSA on this node at all. Defaults to true only on
physical servers whose DMI manufacturer starts with "Dell".

Default value: `(!$facts['is_virtual'] and $facts.dig('dmi', 'manufacturer') =~ /\ADell/`

##### <a name="-omsa--manage_repo"></a>`manage_repo`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to add Dell's package repository (see `omsa::repo`). Set it to
false when the packages come from a repository that's already configured.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-omsa--manage_service"></a>`manage_service`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to manage the OMSA services.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-omsa--package_names"></a>`package_names`

Data type: `Array[String[1], 1]`

OMSA packages to install. The defaults give `omreport` and `omconfig`
with storage support.

Default value: `['srvadmin-base', 'srvadmin-storageservices', 'srvadmin-omcommon']`

##### <a name="-omsa--package_ensure"></a>`package_ensure`

Data type: `String[1]`

`ensure` for the packages: `installed`, `latest`, `absent` or a version.

Default value: `'installed'`

##### <a name="-omsa--service_names"></a>`service_names`

Data type: `Array[String[1]]`

OMSA services to manage.

Default value: `['instsvcdrv', 'dsm_sa_datamgrd', 'dsm_sa_eventmgrd']`

##### <a name="-omsa--service_ensure"></a>`service_ensure`

Data type: `Stdlib::Ensure::Service`

`ensure` for the services.

Default value: `'running'`

##### <a name="-omsa--service_enable"></a>`service_enable`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether the services start at boot.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-omsa--non_dell_certified_flag"></a>`non_dell_certified_flag`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Value of `NonDellCertifiedFlag` in `stsvc.ini`. `true` (OMSA's default)
suppresses alerts for drives that Dell hasn't certified; `false` reports
them. Unset leaves the file alone.

Default value: `undef`

### <a name="omsa--repo"></a>`omsa::repo`

On Debian and Ubuntu an APT source with Dell's key in its own keyring
(`signed-by`); on the Red Hat family a yum repository checked with the same
key, installed in `/etc/pki/rpm-gpg`. The key (fingerprint
`4255 0ABD 1E80 D7C1 BC0B AD85 1285 4914 34D8 786F`) ships with the module.

#### Examples

##### Use another OMSA release on Ubuntu 22.04

```puppet
class { 'omsa::repo':
  apt_location => 'https://linux.dell.com/repo/community/openmanage/11010/jammy',
}
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `omsa::repo` class:

* [`ensure`](#-omsa--repo--ensure)
* [`apt_location`](#-omsa--repo--apt_location)
* [`apt_release`](#-omsa--repo--apt_release)
* [`apt_repos`](#-omsa--repo--apt_repos)
* [`apt_architecture`](#-omsa--repo--apt_architecture)
* [`yum_baseurl`](#-omsa--repo--yum_baseurl)
* [`yum_name`](#-omsa--repo--yum_name)
* [`key_file`](#-omsa--repo--key_file)

##### <a name="-omsa--repo--ensure"></a>`ensure`

Data type: `Enum['present', 'absent']`

`present` or `absent`.

Default value: `'present'`

##### <a name="-omsa--repo--apt_location"></a>`apt_location`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::HTTPUrl]`

APT repository URL.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-omsa--repo--apt_release"></a>`apt_release`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

APT suite. Dell names it after the Ubuntu codename it builds for.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-omsa--repo--apt_repos"></a>`apt_repos`

Data type: `String[1]`

APT component.

Default value: `'main'`

##### <a name="-omsa--repo--apt_architecture"></a>`apt_architecture`

Data type: `String[1]`

Architecture for the APT source. Dell's repository also lists i386, which
has only a few packages.

Default value: `'amd64'`

##### <a name="-omsa--repo--yum_baseurl"></a>`yum_baseurl`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::HTTPUrl]`

Yum repository URL.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-omsa--repo--yum_name"></a>`yum_name`

Data type: `String[1]`

Name of the yum repository.

Default value: `'dell-omsa'`

##### <a name="-omsa--repo--key_file"></a>`key_file`

Data type: `Stdlib::Absolutepath`

Path of Dell's key on the Red Hat family.

Default value: `'/etc/pki/rpm-gpg/RPM-GPG-KEY-dell-omsa'`
